info.name: Hupesi TTS API
info.description:
Public APIs for Hupesi TTS (full docs: {{baseUrl}}/docs).

HOW TO USE
1. Import this file into Postman.
2. Click the collection -> Variables tab: set `baseUrl` (e.g. http://192.168.5.8:8001) and paste your key into `apiKey`.
   Get the key on the machine running the app: Settings -> Allow other machines to access the API (or ~/HupesiTTS/remote-access.json on Linux).
3. Run "Health" first to verify the connection and key.

The key is sent automatically via the X-API-Key header (collection Authorization tab).
When calling from the same machine as the app (127.0.0.1), no key is required.

Audio responses (WAV/MP3): in the Response panel choose Save Response -> Save to a file to listen.

exec: console.warn('401: missing or invalid API key - check the collection apiKey variable.');
console.warn('403: the host machine has not enabled "Allow other machines to access the API", or the app has not been restarted after enabling it.');

request.description: Server status and the currently loaded model (sample_rate, engine, device).
Returns the list of voices: id, name, gender, region, description. Use `id` as voice_id in other APIs.

body.raw:
{
  "text": "Hello, this is Hupesi TTS running on Linux. [pause 1s] Have a great day.",
  "voice_id": "{{voiceId}}",
  "speed": 1.0,
  "temperature": 0.8,
  "format": "wav"
}

request.description:
Returns an audio file. `format`: `wav` or `mp3`. Response headers include X-Duration-Seconds, X-Elapsed-Seconds, X-RTF, X-Sample-Rate.

Pause tags: [pause 2s], [pause 500ms] (or [nghỉ 2s]). Emotion tags (v3 Turbo): [cười], [thở dài].

item.name: 4. Generate speech with subtitles (JSON: base64 audio + SRT)

request.description:
Returns JSON with base64 audio and SRT subtitles with per-sentence timestamps.

Listen and view subtitles in Postman: after Send, open the **Visualize** tab in the Response panel.

Fields: audio_base64, format, sample_rate, duration_seconds, elapsed_seconds, rtf, srt, cues[{start,end,text}].

exec: // Visualize tab: audio player from base64 + subtitle table + .srt download button
{{duration}} s audio · generated in {{elapsed}} s · RTF {{rtf}} · {{sr}} Hz
audio: d.audio_base64, mime, format: d.format, duration: d.duration_seconds,
elapsed: d.elapsed_seconds, rtf: d.rtf, sr: d.sample_rate, cues: d.cues,

url.raw: {{baseUrl}}/stream?text=This is streaming mode; audio is returned in chunks.&voice_id={{voiceId}}

query.value: This is streaming mode; audio is returned in chunks.

request.description:
Chunked WAV: WAV header followed by PCM16 chunks. Postman waits for completion; in a browser/<audio> tag it can play immediately.

The <audio> tag cannot send headers: append `&api_key=<key>` to the URL.
Combines multiple dialogue turns, each with its own voice, into one file.
Each line as `[Name]: line` (or `Name: line`); speaker_mapping maps names to voice_id.
